title: Boyhood clothes, the Buster Brown shoes, and teasing at school
summary: He describes the Norfolk suit, ribbed stockings and heavy shoes every boy wore, his constant runny nose and the hurt of schoolmates saying he smelled, which faded after age seven or eight.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But I let it go, because it wasn't in my realm of thinking. So, all right, I said (unintelligible) and by the way, you see at that time, every young boy at that time had a uniform that he wore. My uniform was a pair of, for Christmas, you get a Norfolk suit of corduroy and you get two pair of stockings, ribbed stockings and they come up to here and then you had a pair of shoes, Buster Brown shoes and had a big toe on them, I hated those big toes and it had a copper on it and laced up and come up -- so then you had to have a cap and then you had long underwear, the underwear was

only covered, went down to -- and you had to learn how to put the underwear in your socks, that big bulge in there and knickers then you did those and you had to get them a certain way, but we found a way and we rolled them so they'd look cute. them a certain way You rolled / so they'd come up real nice, --

No, the pants over the stockings. So now that was -- you had two shirts and the shirts, you had to keep them clean and you had a tie and you had to know how to fix that. That was your uniform, poor me, about the second week the knees was out of those pants and them shoes. I taken a hammer and beat that big knob off of there and then my nose was always running and always sticking out -- cold and my nose running and I was beautiful. I'd come to school and the thing that was happening, I had problems, I think a lot of problems, then the school, the whole thing was--later on, it was suggested or something was said, oh, Jack, smell like pee-peee, hurt my feelings so bad, then they got (unintelligible), somebody smell like pee pee. Oh, my goodness.

And I said, I don't---- but when I passed 7 or 8 years old, it disappeared, so that was -- during that time, everything I'd do, I do all types of things, and my mother says, that's all right, don't worry about it, so everything was beautiful.
